record_body:
Account summary (mid-market, cost-sensitive):
- Pinecone Analytics building customer-facing analytics assistant + internal doc Q&A. Currently using Redwood Hosted API for chat + embeddings; evaluating Redwood Optimize recommendations to reduce $/1k tokens while holding p95 latency.
- Primary theme: they will adopt more aggressive batching/caching/quantization knobs only if changes are versioned, previewable, and reversible quickly.

Current workload / pain points:
- Workload mix: chat completion (streaming) + embeddings batch jobs; intermittent reranking.
- Traffic pattern: weekday peaks; latency-sensitive interactive routes ("/assistant/chat") mixed with background ingestion.
- Target: keep p95 < 900ms at peak for interactive route; cost focus: reduce token cost ~15–25% without quality regressions.

Prior incident (why rollback matters):
- Referenced a previous Optimize-driven config tweak (batching + scheduler tuning) that produced a noticeable latency regression within ~20 minutes after rollout.
- Their phrasing: "We lost an afternoon to chasing what changed." They had to manually back out changes and restart a portion of the fleet; rollback process was unclear/too slow.
- Outcome: they want an explicit config history, easy compare, and one-click rollback to a known-good version with on-call-friendly UX.

Requirements / asks (from calls + notes):
- Safe apply workflow:
  - Diff/preview of what will change (batch size bounds, cache toggles, quant profile, routing policy knobs).
  - Preflight validation: schema + guardrails ("don’t let us set batch size to something that will blow up p95").
  - Canary apply + metric gates (p95 latency, error rate) with automatic halt if gates fail.
- Rollback:
  - One-click rollback to any prior version; clear scope/blast radius (route/model/region/customer).
  - Rollback should be executable by on-call within minutes; include progress + "config converged" signal.
  - Avoid split-brain during partial propagation.
- Auditability (lighter than enterprise but still requested):
  - "Who changed what and when" + linked ticket/justification.
  - Wants exportable audit events (at minimum downloadable view; SIEM export is a nice-to-have).
- Access control:
  - Separate permissions for "apply" vs "rollback" (they want rollback limited to on-call + admins).

Stakeholders (customer side):
- Platform Eng lead (primary technical buyer) + SRE/on-call rotation.
- FinOps partner involved due to cost targets.

Recent activity timeline:
- 2026-01-29: Review call on cost optimization levers; customer flagged prior latency regression and requested "big red rollback button".
- 2026-02-05: SE follow-up: discussed canary gate signals (p95 latency + error rate) and what dashboards we can provide.
- 2026-02-12: Shared draft UX notes for version history/compare/rollback; customer feedback: show blast radius and last-known-good marker.
- 2026-02-18: Customer asked for confirmation on rollout semantics (atomic apply per scope) and how cache invalidation is handled during rollback.

Open questions:
- Whether they will require Dedicated capacity for isolation (they mentioned it as a potential Q2 upgrade if traffic grows), but current evaluation is Hosted + Optimize.
- Whether they need audit log retention controls beyond basic export.

Internal notes:
- Tie-in to project: Safe apply + rollback mechanism is the key unlock for them to expand Optimize usage beyond low-risk routes.
- Reference: SUP-2418 used internally as analogous incident pattern (latency regression after optimization config change).
